claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that all cell lines showed nuclear cisplatin-DNA adducts despite varying apoptotic responses.

claims.claim: Cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines.
claims.source: Furthermore, these cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines (Figure 1C), confirming that pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are also functional across this panel.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by time-course immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are functional across the cell line panel.
claims.source: Furthermore, these cisplatin-DNA adducts progressively resolved over a 72 hr period in all cell lines (Figure 1C), confirming that pathways responsible for facilitating the removal of cisplatin adducts are also functional across this panel.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that cisplatin-DNA adducts resolved over time in all cell lines.

claims.claim: Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse.
claims.source: In line with the detection of cisplatin-DNA adducts (Figure 1C), Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse, followed by a slower wave of Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation in all lines except SW-1573.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation occurred in all lines except SW-1573 following cisplatin pulse.
claims.source: In line with the detection of cisplatin-DNA adducts (Figure 1C), Chk1 (Ser345) phosphorylation increased rapidly in all lines following the 2 hr pulse, followed by a slower wave of Chk2 (Thr68) phosphorylation in all lines except SW-1573.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: In TP53 wildtype cell lines, cisplatin-induced Chk1/Chk2 phosphorylation was followed by p53 phosphorylation and increased expression of MDM2 and p21.
claims.source: Within both the TP53 wildtype cell lines (A549 and SW-1573) this was followed by phosphorylation of p53 (Ser15 and Ser46), the accumulation of total p53 and increased expression of the p53 transcriptional targets MDM2 and p21.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: In TP53 mutant cell lines, p53 phosphorylation occurred but did not result in increased expression of MDM2 or p21.
claims.source: In the TP53 mutant cell lines (NCI-H1573 and NCI-H1975) p53 phosphorylation still occurred, however in line with their loss of DNA binding capability, this did not result in increased expression of MDM2 or p21.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: There was a significant increase in p21 and MDM2 expression in the NCI-H358 line in the absence of p53 expression.
claims.source: Interestingly though, there was a significant increase in p21 and MDM2 expression in the NCI-H358 line in the absence of p53 expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: The first four principal components captured ~70% of variance in the dataset.
claims.source: Using this multi-dimensional analysis, we were able to capture ~70% of variance in the dataset within the first four principal components (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: PC1 and PC2 separated cell lines primarily according to their TP53 status.
claims.source: Unsurprisingly, plotting the first two principal components (PC1 and PC2) against each other (Figure 2A) resulted in separation of the cell lines primarily according to their TP53 status.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: PC3 and PC4 created a clear delineation between the three most resistant cell lines and the three most sensitive lines.
claims.source: However, plotting the third and fourth principal components (PC3 and PC4, Figure 2D,E) created a clear delineation between the three most resistant cell lines (A549, NCI-H358 and NCI-H1573), which cluster towards the left hand side of PC3 (x-axis), and the three most sensitive lines (SW-1573, NCI-1975 and NCI-H1299) which move progressively along PC3 over the 72 hr timeframe.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Cisplatin sensitive cell lines moved along PC3 towards higher levels of γH2A.X, cleaved caspase 3 and stress-associated MAPK signalling.
claims.source: This is in line with the movement of cisplatin sensitive cell lines along PC3 (x-axis) towards higher levels of γH2A.X (H2A.XS139), cleaved caspase 3 and a stress associated MAPK signalling axis (pATF2, pJNK, pc-Jun) (Figure 2D,E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the PCA plot and analyte distribution shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claims.claim: Only the inhibition of P70S6K with dactolisib resulted in a significant increase in cisplatin-induced apoptosis in both A549 and NCI-H358 cell lines.
claims.source: Instead, under these conditions, only the inhibition of P70S6K with the dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor dactolisib resulted in a significant increase in cisplatin-induced apoptosis in both cell lines.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claims.claim: Specific inhibitors of Akt, STAT3, MEK or NF-κB did not significantly increase apoptosis in A549 or NCI-H358 cell lines.
claims.source: Using the resistant A549 (Figure 3C) and NCI-H358 (Figure 3D) cell lines we observed that specific inhibitors of Akt (MK2206), STAT3 (S3I-201), MEK (UO126) or NF- κB (SC-75741) did not significantly increase apoptosis in either cell line, suggesting that while elevated activity of these signalling proteins may be present in one or both of these resistant lines (Figure 2C), they are not causally associated with resistance to cisplatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claims.claim: The lack of sensitisation by an Akt inhibitor suggests a specific role for P70S6K in mediating resistance to cisplatin.
claims.source: While dactolisib will result in the inhibition of a number of substrates downstream of both PI3K and mTOR, the lack of sensitisation by an Akt inhibitor (MK2206) suggests a specific role for P70S6K in mediating resistance to cisplatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential effects of dactolisib and Akt inhibitor on cisplatin sensitivity.

claims.claim: Treatment of the resistant NCI-H358 line with dactolisib increased both caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression to that observed in the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
claims.source: Crucially, treatment of the resistant NCI-H358 line with dactolisib during and after the cisplatin pulse increased both caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression to that observed in the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: P70S6K knockdown with siRNA significantly increased caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression in cisplatin-treated NCI-H358 cells.
claims.source: Under these conditions, cisplatin treatment resulted in significantly higher caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression in the P70S6K knockdown NCI-H358 cells (Figure 3G), whilst P70S6K knockdown did not further sensitise the already cisplatin-sensitive NCI-H1299 cell line (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: P70S6K knockdown significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis in NCI-H358 cells to the same extent as dactolisib treatment.
claims.source: Additionally, P70S6K knockdown with both siRNAs also significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the NCI-H358 cells, to the same extent as that observed with dactolisib treatment (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The combination of carboplatin and dactolisib completely halted tumour growth in NCI-H358 xenografts up to 28 days following a single pulse of carboplatin treatment.
claims.source: However the combination of carboplatin and dactolisib completely halted tumour growth, even up to 28 days following the single pulse of carboplatin treatment.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 3I.

claims.claim: Carboplatin and dactolisib treated xenografts had significantly larger regions of necrosis.
claims.source: Furthermore, an analysis of tumour sections revealed that the carboplatin and dactolisib treated xenografts were not only smaller in size, but also had significantly larger regions of necrosis (Figure 3J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis data shown in Figure 3J.

claims.claim: RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 are amplified or over-expressed in 20% and 11% of lung adenocarcinoma cases, respectively.
claims.source: Indeed, an analysis of TCGA data using cBioPortal (Gao et al., 2013; Cerami et al., 2012; Hoadley et al., 2018) reveals that RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2, the two isoforms of P70S6K, are amplified or over-expressed in 20% and 11% of lung adenocarcinoma cases, respectively (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: TP53 mutations or deletions occur within 47% of lung adenocarcinomas.
claims.source: Importantly, while TP53 mutations or deletions also occur within 47% of lung adenocarcinomas, RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 amplification/over-expression occur on the background of either wildtype or mutant TP53.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Elevated mRNA expression of both RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 isoforms was significantly associated with poor overall survival of lung adenocarcinoma patients.
claims.source: Further analysis with KM plotter (Győrffy et al., 2013) demonstrated that the elevated mRNA expression of both isoforms was also significantly associated with poor overall survival of lung adenocarcinoma patients (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: High expression of P70S6K was significantly associated with poor overall survival in a cohort of 52 lung adenocarcinoma patients.
claims.source: In this cohort, high expression of P70S6K was significantly associated with poor overall survival (Figure 4D), while there was a non-significant trend towards higher P70S6K expression in patients with progressive disease (Figure 4E) and a later disease stage (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and survival analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: P70S6K expression was significantly increased upon relapse in eight patients with matched diagnosis and relapse samples.
claims.source: In eight patients with matched diagnosis and relapse samples, the levels of P70S6K expression were also significantly increased upon relapse (Figure 4G), further highlighting the functional role of P70S6K in the cellular response to platinum therapy.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by IHC analysis of matched patient samples shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: Treatment with a single pulse of cisplatin caused A549 and NCI-H358 cells to be significantly more likely to remain arrested in G1.
claims.source: First, A549 (TP53 wildtype) and NCI-H358 (TP53 null) cells were significantly more likely to remain arrested in G1, both before (G1 arrest before mitosis; ABM) and after undergoing mitosis (G1 arrest after mitosis; AAM) (Figure 5B,C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claims.claim: NCI-H1573 cells did not show any significant increase in G1 transit time following cisplatin treatment.
claims.source: In contrast, NCI-H1573 cells did not show any significant increase in G1 transit time, as may be expected from a TP53 mutant cell line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claims.claim: Cisplatin pulsing resulted in a significant increase in S/G2 transit time for all cell lines.
claims.source: For all cell lines, cisplatin pulsing resulted in a significant increase in S/G2 transit time (Figure 5B,C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claims.claim: NCI-H1573 and NCI-H358 cells delayed for more time in G2 compared to A549 cells after cisplatin treatment.
claims.source: Notably, the NCI-H1573 (TP53 mutant) and NCI-H358 (TP53 null) cells delayed for more time in G2 (G2 arrest; mean 2443 min and 2555 min respectively) compared to A549 cells (mean 1426 min), after which the mutant and null cells often entered a prolonged aberrant mitosis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), resulting in a small increase in cells dying during mitosis or in the following G1/S phase (Figure 5C, death after mitosis; DAM).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Many cisplatin-treated A549 cells turned from green (S/G2) back to red (G1) without undergoing mitosis (G2-exit).
claims.source: In contrast, A549 cells rarely entered into mitosis, instead many of these S/G2 arrested cells turned from green (S/G2) back to red (G1) without undergoing mitosis (G2-exit) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: siRNA-mediated knockdown of p53 in A549 cells resulted in a significant increase in G2-arrest and a decrease in G2-exit.
claims.source: In line with this hypothesis, this orthogonal approach revealed a significant increase in G2-arrest in the p53 knockdown cells, along with a decrease in occurrence of G2-exit, effectively pheno-copying the observed difference between the A549 wildtype and NCI-H358 p53 null cell lines (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data with p53 knockdown shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Treatment of all cell lines with dactolisib as a single agent caused a significant increase in G1 arrest both before and after mitosis, irrespective of TP53 status.
claims.source: Treatment of all cell lines with dactolisib as a single agent also caused a significant increase in G1 arrest both before (G1 ABM) and after mitosis (G1 AAM), irrespective of TP53 status (Figure 5B,C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claims.claim: For TP53 wildtype and null cells in late G1 or S phase at the time of cisplatin pulsing, dactolisib treatment significantly reduced S/G2 transit time and greatly increased apoptosis before mitosis.
claims.source: However, for the TP53 wildtype and null cells that were in late G1 or S phase at the time of cisplatin pulsing, dactolisib treatment significantly reduced S/G2 transit time (Figure 5B) and greatly increased the number of cells that underwent apoptosis before mitosis (Death before mitosis; DBM) (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claims.claim: Dactolisib treatment significantly increased the duration of mitotic arrest, independent of TP53 status.
claims.source: Notably, dactolisib treatment did not prevent cisplatin treated cells from entering into an aberrant mitosis, but did significantly increase the duration of mitotic arrest, independent of TP53 status (Figure 5B), which correlated with an increase in death during or after mitosis (DAM) in TP53 wildtype and null, but not mutant cells (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and 5D.

claims.claim: Dactolisib treatment did not result in any sensitisation of TP53 mutant H1573 cells to cisplatin.
claims.source: Surprisingly, dactolisib treatment did not result in any sensitisation of TP53 mutant H1573 cells to cisplatin (Figure 5D), which also corresponded with a failure of dactolisib to significantly reduce S/G2 phase transit time (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5B and 5D.

claims.claim: siRNA-mediated P70S6K knockdown in NCI-H358 cells resulted in a non-significant trend towards a shortened G2-arrest and greatly increased cell death both before or after mitosis.
claims.source: This approach demonstrated that specific ablation of P70S6K in this model resulted in a non-significant trend towards a shortened G2-arrest with both P70S6K siRNAs, and a greatly increased cell death both before (DBM) or after mitosis (DAM).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data with P70S6K knockdown shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: There was increased expression of p21 following cisplatin treatment in the resistant NCI-H358 line, but not the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
claims.source: While both the NCI-H1299 and NCI-H358 cell lines are TP53 null, there was an increased expression of p21 following cisplatin treatment in the resistant NCI-H358 line, but not the sensitive NCI-H1299 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: The increased p21 expression by NCI-H358 cells was efficiently inhibited by both treatment with dactolisib and the specific knockdown of P70S6K with siRNA.
claims.source: Importantly, the increased p21 expression by NCI-H358 cells was also observed by western blotting of independent samples and was efficiently inhibited by both treatment with dactolisib (Figure 6A,B) and the specific knockdown of P70S6K with siRNA (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A, 6B, and 6C.

claims.claim: p63 is elevated in the NCI-H358 line following treatment with cisplatin, and is inhibited by the addition of dactolisib or treatment with P70S6K siRNA.
claims.source: However, in the absence of p53, we observed that this may potentially be mediated by the related transcription factor p63, which is elevated in the NCI-H358 line following treatment with cisplatin, and also inhibited by the addition of dactolisib (Figure 6A,B) or treatment with P70S6K siRNA (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6A, 6B, and 6C.

claims.claim: Both TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition of dactolisib.
claims.source: In accordance with this hypothesis, and in line with the FUCCI single-cell imaging (Figure 5A), both the TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition dactolisib, as was the resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358 (Figures 2D, H and 6D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: The resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358, was significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition of dactolisib.
claims.source: In accordance with this hypothesis, and in line with the FUCCI single-cell imaging (Figure 5A), both the TP53 wildtype cell lines were significantly sensitised to cisplatin by the addition dactolisib, as was the resistant TP53 null line, NCI-H358 (Figures 2D, H and 6D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573.
claims.source: Also, in line with the FUCCI analysis, dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573, whilst it significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Dactolisib significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
claims.source: Also, in line with the FUCCI analysis, dactolisib was not able to increase cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant line NCI-H1573, whilst it significantly antagonised cisplatin-induced apoptosis in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1975 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: The addition of dactolisib to the TP53 wildtype A549 cell line inhibited cisplatin-induced p53 and p21 accumulation, resulting in elevated markers of DNA damage and apoptosis.
claims.source: In line with this hypothesis, the addition of dactolisib to the TP53 wildtype A549 cell line inhibited cisplatin-induced p53 and p21 accumulation, resulting in elevated markers of DNA damage (γH2A.X expression) and apoptosis (caspase 3 cleavage) following cisplatin treatment (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: In the TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 line, p21 expression was not significantly elevated following cisplatin treatment, and γH2A.X expression and caspase 3 cleavage were unchanged by the addition of dactolisib.
claims.source: However, in the TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 line, which was not sensitised by dactolisib, p21 expression was not significantly elevated following cisplatin treatment, and γH2A.X expression and caspase 3 cleavage were unchanged by the addition of dactolisib (Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 6E (referenced as Figure 7 in the text).

claims.claim: A strong correlation was observed between phosphorylated P70S6K levels and decreased apoptosis in response to cisplatin for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092).
claims.source: However, the strength of this correlation was greatly increased when considering the TP53 status of the lines, with a strong correlation observed for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092) but no correlation for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: No correlation was observed between phosphorylated P70S6K levels and apoptosis in response to cisplatin for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
claims.source: However, the strength of this correlation was greatly increased when considering the TP53 status of the lines, with a strong correlation observed for wildtype TP53 lines (r2 = 0.6092) but no correlation for TP53 mutant lines (r2 = 0.1764).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line.
claims.source: In agreement with our finding that elevated P70S6K activity promotes resistance in a TP53 dependent manner, combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line, but not the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6H.

claims.claim: Combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib did not sensitise the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
claims.source: In agreement with our finding that elevated P70S6K activity promotes resistance in a TP53 dependent manner, combination therapy with cisplatin and dactolisib significantly sensitised the high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cell line, but not the high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 line.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6H.

claims.claim: P70S6K promotes an aberrant G2-exit or prolonged G2-arrest following cisplatin treatment through enhanced translation of p53/p21 in TP53 wildtype cell lines and p63/p21 in TP53 null lines.
claims.source: Therefore, this data demonstrates that P70S6K promotes an aberrant G2-exit or prolonged G2-arrest following cisplatin treatment, presumably through enhanced translation of p53/p21 in TP53 wildtype cell lines and p63/p21 in TP53 null lines (Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data on P70S6K effects on cell cycle, p21 expression, and TP53 status-dependent responses.

claims.claim: In the presence of mutant p53, P70S6K is not able to influence the DNA damage induced signalling axis and is therefore not associated with sensitivity to cisplatin.
claims.source: However, in the presence of mutant p53, P70S6K is not able to influence this DNA damage induced signalling axis and is therefore not associated with sensitivity to cisplatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that dactolisib does not sensitize TP53 mutant cells to cisplatin.

claims.claim: Continuous culturing of cells in the presence of high doses of platinum drugs in vitro would result in the accumulation of numerous off-target adducts and the activation of a stress response incongruent with the actual in vivo apoptotic mechanism.
claims.source: It is likely that the continuous culturing of cells in the presence of high doses of these drugs in vitro would result in the accumulation of numerous off-target adducts and the activation of a stress response incongruent with the actual in vivo apoptotic mechanism.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of continuous and pulsed cisplatin treatment models.

claims.claim: p38 activity is induced by the continuous exposure model, but not by the pulse model.
claims.source: Indeed, this effect may be apparent in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D/2, where p38 activity is induced by the continuous exposure model, but not by the pulse model.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Highly elevated p38 signalling was not observed in any cell line following the cisplatin pulse.
claims.source: A number of previous studies have implicated the activity of p38 in mediating resistance to cisplatin (Sarin et al., 2018; Pereira et al., 2013; Galan-Moya et al., 2011; Hernández Losa et al., 2003), however we did not observe highly elevated p38 signalling in any cell line following the cisplatin pulse (Figure 1D), nor a correlation between p38 activity and the apoptotic response (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiplexed protein analysis data shown in Figure 1D and the PCA analysis in Figure 2.

claims.claim: High levels of P70S6K expression have previously been associated with aggressive tumour behaviour in lung cancer.
claims.source: High levels of P70S6K expression have previously been associated with aggressive tumour behaviour in lung cancer (Chen et al., 2017), as well as other cancer types such as breast (Holz, 2012), colorectal (Nozawa et al., 2007) and liver (Sahin et al., 2004) cancers.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2017, Holz, 2012, Nozawa et al., 2007, and Sahin et al., 2004.

claims.claim: P70S6K can regulate cell cycle progression via the enhanced translation of p21 mRNA.
claims.source: Further supporting this central role of P70S6K, previous research has demonstrated that P70S6K can regulate cell cycle progression via the enhanced translation of p21 mRNA (Guégan et al., 2014), although our data also suggest that P70S6K may also play a role in the enhanced expression of both p53 and p63 in this context.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guégan et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The combination of cisplatin and dactolisib has previously been proposed for osteosarcoma, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and bladder cancer.
claims.source: The combination of cisplatin and dactolisib has also previously been proposed for osteosarcoma (Huang et al., 2018), head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (Hsu et al., 2018) and bladder cancer (Moon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2018, Hsu et al., 2018, and Moon et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The failure of many clinical trials is frequently attributed to the lack of suitable biomarkers to stratify the patient cohort.
claims.source: This fine grained stratification of response is an important finding, as the failure of many clinical trials is frequently attributed to the lack of suitable biomarkers to stratify the patient cohort (Hay et al., 2014), highlighting the value of our approach that is capable of dissecting the mechanism of variable drug response across differing genetic backgrounds.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hay et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The inability of dactolisib to regulate p21 expression in TP53 mutant tumour cells following cisplatin treatment likely underlies the inability of dactolisib to sensitise these cells to cisplatin.
claims.source: The inability of dactolisib to regulate p21 expression in TP53 mutant tumour cells following cisplatin treatment likely underlies the inability of dactolisib to sensitise these cells to cisplatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined observations of p21 regulation and sensitization patterns across different TP53 backgrounds.

claims.claim: Within the context of a potential clinical trial for cisplatin and dactolisib combination, the TP53 mutation status of each patient tumour would be a central consideration for identification of the most effective treatment strategy.
claims.source: Therefore, within the context of a potential clinical trial for this drug combination, the TP53 mutation status of each patient tumour would be a central consideration for identification of the most effective treatment strategy and an understanding of individual patient response.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the TP53-dependent effects of dactolisib on cisplatin sensitivity.

claims.claim: Platinum therapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication.
claims.source: As platinum chemotherapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication, the progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis (Jamieson and Lippard, 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jamieson and Lippard, 1999.

claims.claim: The progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis following platinum chemotherapy.
claims.source: As platinum chemotherapies work by forming covalent DNA adducts, which distort the DNA helix and block replication, the progressive accumulation of single stranded and double stranded breaks is thought to induce apoptosis (Jamieson and Lippard, 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jamieson and Lippard, 1999.

claims.claim: A G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21.
claims.source: A similar G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21 (Gire and Dulic, 2015) and likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gire and Dulic, 2015.

claims.claim: G2-exit likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
claims.source: A similar G2-exit, senescence state has been reported to be dependent on p21 (Gire and Dulic, 2015) and likely provides TP53 wildtype cells protection from death by preventing progression through an aberrant mitosis.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of G2-exit in TP53 wildtype cells and its association with reduced apoptosis.

claims.claim: In TP53 wildtype A549 cells, dactolisib induced pre-mitotic cell death and prevented cells from undergoing a protective G2-exit.
claims.source: In the TP53 wildtype A549 cells it induced pre-mitotic cell death and prevented cells from undergoing a protective G2-exit, which is likely partially dependent on the p53-p21 axis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: In the TP53 null NCI-H358 line, dactolisib promoted both pre-mitotic cell death and the entry of cells into a prolonged deleterious aberrant mitosis.
claims.source: Similarly, in the TP53 null line, dactolisib promoted both pre-mitotic cell death and the entry of cells into a prolonged deleterious aberrant mitosis, the latter likely due to a weakened p53-dependent G2 checkpoint (Engeland, 2018).

results.result: The manuscript provides background on lung adenocarcinoma epidemiology, treatment challenges, and platinum resistance, citing that lung adenocarcinoma is the most common form of lung cancer and the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy remaining below 30% despite over 147 proposed resistance mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C8 are all supported by appropriate citations to prior literature and represent well-established background knowledge in the field. These claims provide context for the study but are not novel findings from the current work.

results.result: The authors justify their cisplatin pulse model by citing pharmacokinetic studies showing that cisplatin and carboplatin are rapidly cleared from circulation and tumors within 2-3 hours in humans and rodents.
results.evaluation: Claims C9 and C86 are supported by appropriate citations (Andersson et al., 1996; Johansen et al., 2002) and provide the rationale for the experimental model design. This is a methodological justification rather than a novel finding.

results.result: Continuous cisplatin exposure resulted in decreased cell number, increased apoptosis, and elevated DNA damage response compared to pulsed treatment in A549 cells, with distinct signaling patterns including p38/ERK activation in continuous exposure and MCL-1 expression in pulsed treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C14 and C70 are supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging, viability assays, and multiplexed protein analysis (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2). The data clearly demonstrate differential responses between continuous and pulsed cisplatin treatment models. Claim C69 is an inference that is reasonable given the data.

results.result: Across a panel of six lung adenocarcinoma cell lines, the apoptotic response to cisplatin pulse ranged from ~3% (A549) to ~32% (NCI-H1299), and this sensitivity could not be stratified simply by TP53 mutation status.
results.evaluation: Claims C15 and C16 are supported by apoptosis measurements shown in Figure 1B. The data clearly show a range of responses that do not correlate simply with TP53 status, which is a key finding that motivates the subsequent mechanistic investigation.

results.result: All six cell lines displayed significant nuclear cisplatin-DNA adducts following a 2-hour pulse that progressively resolved over 72 hours, suggesting that drug efflux and DNA repair pathways are functional across the panel and not responsible for differential sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C20 are supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3). The inference that drug efflux is not responsible for differential sensitivity (C18, C20) is reasonable given that all lines show similar adduct formation and resolution, though alternative explanations are not fully excluded.

results.result: Following cisplatin pulse, Chk1 and Chk2 phosphorylation increased in most cell lines, with TP53 wildtype lines showing subsequent p53 phosphorylation and increased MDM2/p21 expression, while TP53 mutant lines showed p53 phosphorylation without MDM2/p21 induction, and the TP53 null NCI-H358 line showed increased p21/MDM2 expression despite lacking p53.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C25 are supported by multiplexed protein analysis data (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4). The data clearly demonstrate TP53 status-dependent signaling responses. The unexpected p21/MDM2 expression in NCI-H358 (C25) is particularly interesting and is followed up later in the manuscript.

results.result: Principal component analysis of cisplatin-induced signaling dynamics captured ~70% of variance in the first four components, with PC1/PC2 separating cell lines by TP53 status and PC3/PC4 delineating resistant versus sensitive lines, with sensitive lines moving toward higher γH2A.X, cleaved caspase 3, and stress-associated MAPK signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C29 are supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A. The analysis appropriately captures variance and provides a data-driven approach to identify signaling patterns associated with sensitivity. The interpretation is consistent with the visualizations provided.

results.result: Among tested inhibitors of Akt, STAT3, MEK, NF-κB, and P70S6K, only the dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor dactolisib (which inhibits P70S6K) significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis in resistant A549 and NCI-H358 cell lines, suggesting a specific role for P70S6K in mediating resistance.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C32 are supported by apoptosis assay data (Figure 3C and 3D). The specificity for dactolisib over other pathway inhibitors is clearly demonstrated. However, claim C32 involves an inference about P70S6K specificity that is later validated with siRNA experiments, making this result well-supported overall.

results.result: Dactolisib treatment or P70S6K siRNA knockdown in resistant NCI-H358 cells increased caspase 3 cleavage and γH2A.X expression to levels observed in sensitive NCI-H1299 cells, and significantly increased cisplatin-induced apoptosis to the same extent as dactolisib treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C35 are supported by western blotting (Figure 3E, 3G) and apoptosis assay data (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). The siRNA validation is critical for establishing P70S6K as the specific target responsible for the dactolisib effect, and the data clearly support this conclusion.

results.result: In NCI-H358 xenografts, carboplatin alone had no significant effect on tumor growth, dactolisib alone had a moderate effect, but the combination completely halted tumor growth up to 28 days and resulted in significantly larger regions of necrosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C36, C37, C93, and C94 are supported by in vivo xenograft data (Figure 3I) and histological analysis (Figure 3J). The data clearly demonstrate synergistic effects of the combination therapy. Statistical significance is reported for the combination versus single agents.

results.result: Analysis of TCGA data reveals that RPS6KB1 and RPS6KB2 (encoding P70S6K isoforms) are amplified or over-expressed in 20% and 11% of lung adenocarcinoma cases respectively, occurring on backgrounds of both wildtype and mutant TP53 (which is mutated/deleted in 47% of cases).
results.evaluation: Claims C38, C39, and C90 are supported by TCGA data analysis shown in Figure 4A. The analysis appropriately uses publicly available data to establish clinical relevance. The co-occurrence with different TP53 backgrounds is important for the subsequent findings about TP53-dependent effects.

results.result: Elevated RPS6KB1/RPS6KB2 mRNA expression was significantly associated with poor overall survival in lung adenocarcinoma patients, and in a cohort of 52 patients, high P70S6K protein expression was significantly associated with poor survival and was significantly increased upon relapse in matched samples.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C42 are supported by survival analysis from KM plotter (Figure 4B) and IHC analysis of patient samples (Figure 4D, 4G). The matched diagnosis/relapse samples (n=8) showing increased P70S6K at relapse provide particularly strong evidence for functional relevance. Statistical significance is reported for the survival associations.

results.result: FUCCI live-cell imaging revealed that cisplatin pulse caused TP53 wildtype (A549) and null (NCI-H358) cells to arrest in G1 and increased S/G2 transit time in all lines, with TP53 mutant/null cells showing prolonged G2 arrest and aberrant mitosis, while A549 cells underwent G2-exit without mitosis; p53 knockdown in A549 cells increased G2-arrest and decreased G2-exit.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C48 are supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data (Figure 5B, 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and 2). The single-cell tracking provides detailed cell cycle dynamics. The p53 knockdown experiment (C48) validates the role of p53 in the G2-exit phenotype. The data are quantitative and statistically analyzed.

results.result: Dactolisib treatment increased G1 arrest in all cell lines regardless of TP53 status, but for TP53 wildtype/null cells in late G1/S phase during cisplatin pulse, dactolisib reduced S/G2 transit time and greatly increased pre-mitotic apoptosis and prolonged mitotic arrest; however, dactolisib did not sensitize TP53 mutant H1573 cells, and P70S6K knockdown in NCI-H358 cells showed similar effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C53 are supported by FUCCI live-cell imaging data (Figure 5B, 5C, 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 3). The data clearly demonstrate TP53 status-dependent effects of dactolisib on cell cycle and apoptosis. The P70S6K siRNA validation (C53) confirms specificity, though the effect on G2-arrest was non-significant, which is appropriately noted.

results.result: The resistant TP53 null NCI-H358 line showed increased p21 expression following cisplatin (unlike sensitive NCI-H1299), which was efficiently inhibited by dactolisib or P70S6K siRNA; p63 was also elevated in NCI-H358 after cisplatin and inhibited by dactolisib or P70S6K siRNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C56 are supported by multiplexed protein analysis (Figure 1D) and western blotting (Figure 6A, 6B, 6C). The data clearly show differential p21 expression between resistant and sensitive TP53 null lines, and the regulation by P70S6K. The p63 finding (C56) is interesting but somewhat speculative regarding mechanism.

results.result: Both TP53 wildtype cell lines and the resistant TP53 null NCI-H358 line were significantly sensitized to cisplatin by dactolisib, while dactolisib did not increase apoptosis in TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 and significantly antagonized apoptosis in TP53 mutant NCI-H1975.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C60 are supported by apoptosis assay data (Figure 6D). The data clearly demonstrate TP53 status-dependent effects of dactolisib sensitization. The antagonistic effect in NCI-H1975 (C60) is particularly important for understanding the limitations of the combination therapy.

results.result: In TP53 wildtype A549 cells, dactolisib inhibited cisplatin-induced p53 and p21 accumulation, resulting in elevated γH2A.X and caspase 3 cleavage; however, in TP53 mutant NCI-H1573 cells, p21 was not significantly elevated by cisplatin and γH2A.X/caspase 3 were unchanged by dactolisib.
results.evaluation: Claims C61 and C62 are supported by western blotting data (Figure 6E). The data clearly show differential effects of dactolisib based on TP53 status and p21 regulation, providing a mechanistic explanation for the differential sensitization observed.

results.result: In a secondary panel of lung adenocarcinoma cell lines, a strong correlation (r²=0.6092) was observed between phosphorylated P70S6K levels and decreased apoptosis for TP53 wildtype lines but no correlation (r²=0.1764) for TP53 mutant lines; combination therapy sensitized high pP70S6K/TP53 wildtype NCI-H292 cells but not high pP70S6K/TP53 mutant NCI-H2009 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C66 are supported by correlation analysis (Figure 6G) and apoptosis assays (Figure 6H) in an independent panel of cell lines. This validation in additional cell lines strengthens the conclusion about TP53-dependent effects. The correlation coefficients are appropriate for the sample sizes, though the TP53 wildtype correlation is moderate.

results.result: The authors conclude that P70S6K promotes G2-exit or prolonged G2-arrest following cisplatin through enhanced translation of p53/p21 in TP53 wildtype lines and p63/p21 in TP53 null lines, but in TP53 mutant cells, P70S6K cannot influence the DNA damage signaling axis and is not associated with cisplatin sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C67, C68, and C76 represent integrative conclusions drawn from multiple lines of evidence including cell cycle analysis, protein expression, and sensitization experiments. The conclusions are well-supported by the data, though the p63 mechanism in TP53 null cells (C67) is somewhat speculative and would benefit from additional validation.

results.result: The authors propose that TP53 mutation status should be a central consideration for patient stratification in potential clinical trials of cisplatin and dactolisib combination therapy.
results.evaluation: Claim C77 is a reasonable inference based on the demonstrated TP53-dependent effects of dactolisib sensitization. This represents an important translational implication of the findings, though it is a recommendation for future work rather than a direct experimental result.

results.result: Highly elevated p38 signaling was not observed in any cell line following cisplatin pulse, and JNK inhibition did not prevent cisplatin-induced apoptosis in SW-1573 cells, suggesting these pathways are not promoting apoptosis in this context.
results.evaluation: Claims C71, C95, and C96 are supported by multiplexed protein analysis (Figure 1D, Figure 2) and apoptosis assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C). These negative results are important for distinguishing the pulse model from continuous exposure and for ruling out alternative mechanisms.

results.result: The manuscript cites established mechanisms of platinum therapy action (DNA adduct formation leading to DNA breaks and apoptosis) and p21-dependent G2-exit/senescence that provides protection from aberrant mitosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C81 are supported by appropriate citations to prior literature (Jamieson and Lippard, 1999; Gire and Dulic, 2015) and represent established background knowledge used to interpret the current findings.

results.result: The authors describe distinct mechanisms by which dactolisib sensitizes cells to cisplatin depending on TP53 status: in TP53 wildtype cells it induces pre-mitotic death and prevents protective G2-exit; in TP53 null cells it promotes pre-mitotic death and prolonged aberrant mitosis; in TP53 mutant cells there is no sensitization due to sustained S/G2 arrest; and dactolisib treatment in early G1 results in G1 arrest and reduced apoptosis, highlighting the importance of DNA replication.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C85 represent summary interpretations of the FUCCI imaging data (Figure 5) and are well-supported by the experimental evidence. These mechanistic insights explain the TP53-dependent effects observed in the apoptosis assays.

results.result: The manuscript cites prior literature establishing that P70S6K expression is associated with aggressive tumor behavior and poor prognosis in multiple cancers, that P70S6K regulates cell cycle via p21 translation, that cisplatin/dactolisib combinations have been proposed for other cancers, and that clinical trial failures are often attributed to lack of biomarkers for patient stratification.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C75, C87-C89, and C91 are all supported by appropriate citations to prior literature and provide context for the current findings. These represent established knowledge rather than novel results from this study.
